notes.title: The Ruler's Manual #7 - War
notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings, mighty Builders! 🏛️ [/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Any ruler who wants to [b]go down in history[/b] 📚 should get acquainted with the "Ruler's Manual" series! Why - you ask? Well, in the following entries we tell you about how to make your Polis wealthy, safe, and as prosperous as possible. And believe us, it's [b]not as easy as it may seem! [/b]


[hr][/hr]
[url=https://discord.gg/8KnCYpm2xT][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/2457a52332739537a74a64a1369ff6b89f30a2d4.png[/img][/url]
[hr][/hr]
[h3]...and talk to the community and developers about the game![/h3]


Since the dawn of time, social groups, clans, or tribes [b]attacked their neighbors[/b] in order to grab their resources, land, or treasures. The situation is no different in the case of your Polis - you can be sure that sooner or later foreign forces will want to take some of your wealth for themselves ✊ Of course you, a competent ruler, [b]cannot allow that to happen![/b] Today you will learn how to defend your city and its inhabitants and how to prepare a loyal army of brave soldiers. Here we go!


[h2]The invaders are on the horizon[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
You can be sure that the enemy rulers are watching the development of your Polis with envy and great interest. At some point, they will decide that your influence or wealth should be limited and will [b]send their troops to your territory[/b] 💰 And that never bodes well...

The enemy [b]attack can be carried out both from land and sea[/b], so you always have to be on your guard. Left alone, the invaders can quickly spread across your city and do a lot of damage - and this is something you can't let happen! Repairing the harm they did can be very time-consuming and costly, not to mention a hostile attack can trigger a wave of famine or emigration 💥 On the other hand, successfully repelling attacks can guarantee your city relative peace and undisturbed development.
So how do you protect your loyal subjects from looting and violence? [b]You will need an army![/b]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/48bfeef281c24eaa34b9d957d7a40aa9568af639.png[/img]


[h2]Building an army[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
When your settlement transforms from a small village into a more and more advanced town, it's time to consider rising your own army. The most important element at this stage will be people, as in order to form your first squad [b]you will need recruits[/b] 📝 The good thing is that all adult inhabitants of your Polis can become such recruits and find their way to the barracks. Of course, the bigger your city's population, the better - strength often lies in numbers!

The next stage of creating units is to provide your warriors with[b] appropriate equipment[/b]. Depending on whether you choose light infantry units, ranged units, or powerful, heavily armored elite units, the cost of equipping them will be different. Remember to find a [b]balance between your spending on building an army and the budget for developing the city[/b] - both of these elements should complement each other. Once you manage to pay for the equipment of your warriors, it's time to train them. In this case, the principle is similar - the more advanced the type of unit, the longer it takes to train them.

[h2]Make your own strategic choices[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
While smaller settlements do not have much choice when it comes to the types of troops they can recruit, large, developed cities have full freedom here. It is worth noting that a [b]more diverse range of troops at your command[/b] means not only more effective defense, but also the ability to match your current army to the state of your empire's economy. If you do well as a ruler, you will soon gain access to buildings such as Barracks, Archery Range 🏹, Walls, Gates, Watchtowers, War Machine Workshops, or Cavalry Stable! 🐴


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/677343280110607da88fc83e0e6f2ab9b6237a1c.jpg[/img]


Having a strong army, however, is not only a privilege, but also an obligation. Make no mistake, your [b]soldiers need to eat, have access to services, medicine, and so on, [/b]even in times of peace. Sometimes having too many warriors can overwhelm your economy and production capacity, on the other hand having a small army unable to cope with invaders is quite risky. Once again, [b]key decisions regarding your empire are yours[/b]. Will you be able to build a strong, battle-seasoned army? Can you protect your subjects from enemy attacks? notes.title: Architect's Corner #8 - Baths and Academy
notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings Builders! 🏛️ [/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Welcome to the next part of our "Architect's Corner" series, in which we tell you all about [b]the buildings you will have at your disposal as a ruler of an ancient Greek Polis[/b]. Discover interesting tips and tricks, learn how to effectively plan the development of your city, and check out how many useful structures you can raise - all this to the glory of a great ruler, such as yourself! 👑


[url=https://discord.gg/8KnCYpm2xT][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/2457a52332739537a74a64a1369ff6b89f30a2d4.png[/img][/url]
[h3]...and talk to the community and developers about the game![/h3]


[h2]Achievements of the ancient Greek civilization[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Ancient Greece can boast of many great achievements, such as deep philosophies, geometry, or democracy. Among many others, we can also list [b]the architecture[/b]. Today we will look at two magnificent structures that will prove that erecting breathtaking (and at the same time useful) buildings was their forte. All right! Grab your pen, scrolls, and... a towel!

[h2]Useful and pleasant - the Baths 🧼[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Ancient Greeks cared about their appearance and health (which was, in a way, the basis of their philosophy), so naturally, they also had to [b]take a good care of their hygiene.[/b] Our today's first building helps them in this task. Let's take a look at magnificent, steamy Baths and check out how they can benefit your city.

As you can see, the Baths is a quite big and intriguing building. The entrance is decorated with ornaments, statues, and columns, and the roof is covered with red tiles. In its center, however, there is an exposed courtyard. Throughout the day, the Baths is filled with the [b]sounds of conversations and splashing water.[/b] 💦 We mean... who wouldn't want to jump into the relaxing, clear water after long hours of work? Your subjects, weary of hard labor, can visit this facility to take a bath and improve their hygiene.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/e70a26d3103483f255cd9466042d0b4a1fadccb8.png[/img]


Maintaining high standards of[b] hygiene is extremely important for the well-being of your city[/b] and its inhabitants. If you are struggling with maintaining cleanliness, your citizens will soon catch some nasty diseases that may prove fatal to them. Of course, the Baths is just one way to improve the quality of hygiene in your Polis, but it is definitely one of the most effective! Remember - a clean population is a healthy population.


[h2]Welcome to the Academy - the domain of philosophy and science 📖[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
The history of Ancient Greece is full of great thinkers, philosophers, and inventors. The masters had their disciples, who in turn trained other scholars. But where did it all take place? The answer is... the Academy - the domain of[b] philosophy and science.[/b] 📜 Let's take a peek at the brightest minds of the era and see what they're working on this time!

If philosophers and thinkers find your city an attractive place to settle, then the aforementioned Academy will be very, very useful to you. After meeting the appropriate conditions, the greatest theories and ideas will arise within its walls! Thanks to the work of the Academy, you will receive the [b]so-called Research Points[/b], which you can use to discover new technologies and solutions. As a ruler, you will have to analyze the current situation of your empire and decide which ones are most important and should be prioritized. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/7914ead77265e4998bf2438f0f3df7852d79962e.png[/img]


Your city can develop to some extent without the help of the Academy, but in the later stages of the game, it will get [b]more and more difficult[/b]. Remember to take care of the intellectual growth of your Polis and its inhabitants, for the common good. Thanks to the wise disposal of Research Points, you will gain access to[b] new buildings and opportunities[/b] - the sooner it happens, the better! 

In the following parts of the series, we will return with [b]descriptions of many other cool structures [/b]that will ensure the safety, well-being, and development of your city. We hope that the buildings presented today will find their place among the streets of your Polis, and that they will contribute to the growth of [b]your magnificent empire![/b] 😀 As always - thank you and stay tuned!

Welcome to the next part of our "Architect's Corner" series, in which we tell you all about [b]the buildings you will have at your disposal as a ruler of an ancient Greek Polis[/b]. Discover interesting tips and tricks, learn how to effectively plan the development of your city, and check out how many useful structures you can raise - all this to the glory of a great ruler, such as yourself! 👑

[h3]...and talk to the community and developers about the game![/h3]



[h2]A sneak peek at the huts of two extraordinary craftsmen[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Today we will visit two quiet workplaces that, while seemingly very different, have a few common elements. Both of them are somewhat [b]necessary for the life of your subjects[/b] and have a positive impact on their well-being and sense of security.

That being said, let's find out why you should consider building a Cheesemaker's hut and Herbalist's hut in your city and [b]how they actually work to produce valuable goods[/b]. You can be sure that your community will be happy to have one of them in their neighborhood 😉 And as we all know, one of your goals is to keep them happy, isn't it?

[h2]Cheesemaker's hut 🧀[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Cheese belongs to a much more advanced food category than basic foods like fish or game meat, which means it is generally more desirable and liked by your subjects. [b]No wonder![/b] As it is well known, [b]cheese is tasty, nutritious, and healthy.[/b] 🍴 That is why it is so important that it regularly finds its way to the tables of your citizens to keep them fed and improve their mood and satisfaction. But how is cheese made? And what is needed to produce it? Let's reveal some of the Cheesemaker secrets!

In order for the Cheesemakers to start their work (in addition to building their hut!), you need to provide them with the [b]required resources[/b]. These resources are milk produced on a goat farm and linen, woven in a loom. Thus equipped, the craftsmen can begin preparing their specialties. Thanks to their experience, skills, the right tools, and patience, [b]the peculiar smell of cheese[/b] will soon waft over their hut 👃 Only the inhabitants of more advanced towns possess the proprer technology to place this building, so know that it will not be available from the beginning of your adventure in Builders of Greece. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/bd428da2d7b7919337f3b62576cf96133281517d.png[/img]


It is worth noting that providing your population with various types of food [b]improves their well-being,[/b] and cheese can certainly be counted on in this aspect 😊 So don't hesitate! Develop the right technology, find a convenient place, and order your subjects to build a Cheesemaker's hut [b]for the common good of your Polis![/b]


[h2]Herbalist's hut 🌿[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Ahh... let's take a moment to relax in the garden. And not just in any garden, but the workplace of Herbalists. Their peaceful hut is surrounded by flower beds where [b]all sorts of plants grow[/b]. The whole area is surrounded by a wooden fence to protect it from danger and harm 🍃 There is also a cellar that was built in front of the hut to dry, collect, and prepare the herbs for further use. Lovely, isn't it?

The main task of herbalists is, of course, growing and harvesting herbs. At first glance, it looks quite trivial, but you must be aware that [b]herbs are very important to the prosperity of your city.[/b] Thanks to these awesome plants, pharmacists are able to produce medicines that help improve the health of sick people 🤧 If it weren't for the herbs, [b]diseases could spread in your Polis[/b], which could lead to an outbreak of epidemics! The health of the population is one of the most important factors that affects the proper development of your city - [b]remember not to underestimate it and guarantee it a proper deal of your attention![/b]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/227df9943df802bf8e0c323e29ee3df0f68cf0cf.png[/img]


However, a herb garden left to itself, without caring hands to nurture it, would quickly overgrow with weeds, unwanted shrubs, and grasses. Fortunately, in this situation, [b]you can count on the Herbalist. Let's see... [/b]there is a sharp sickle hanging at his waist, a leather bag thrown over his shoulder, and his head is full of the knowledge of all kinds of vegetation and plants 🌱 

[b]Their daily tasks include tending the garden and collecting mature herbs[/b]. It seems a fairly simple job, but make no mistake - without proper preparation and experience it would be virtually impossible to perform. Plant knowledge is passed down from generation to generation and is a very important aspect when it comes to the health of your population. Herbalists are people who are not afraid to get their hands dirty 🤲 and work on their knees if the situation requires it. Many of them say that their greatest reward is the undeniable [b]contribution to the well-being of the city [/b]and seeing their loved ones and neighbors in good health. Way to go, guys!

notes.title: The Ruler's Manual #6 - Food and Hunger
notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings, mighty Builders! 🏛️ [/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Any ruler who wants to [b]go down in history[/b] 📚 should get acquainted with the "Ruler's Manual" series! Why - you ask? Well, in the following entries we tell you about how to make your Polis wealthy, safe, and as prosperous as possible. And believe us, it's [b]not as easy as it may seem! [/b]


[url=https://discord.gg/8KnCYpm2xT][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/2457a52332739537a74a64a1369ff6b89f30a2d4.png[/img][/url]
[h3]...and talk to the community and developers about the game![/h3]



[h2]A few facts about the bellies of your subjects[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Make no mistake, the subject of the abundance of your granaries and storehouses should not be taken lightly. In the past, [b]many great empires collapsed[/b] due to crop failure, famine, and related riots or diseases 💀 And it is no different with the city that you will manage! The empty bellies of your subjects mean trouble - that's one of the golden rules that every wise ruler, like you, takes into account. On the other hand, well-fed, satisfied citizens will surely repay you with their hard work and obedience. You are about to learn how to achieve this favorable state of affairs and how to ensure that their tables are never empty!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/46bad59f0fc4cabd45195a44037303e7495e3553.gif[/img]

Providing food for your citizens should be your priority from the very beginning of your reign. While they can do without comforts, access to luxuries, entertainment, or culture (at least for some time), [b]hunger will quickly make them leave your city[/b]... or simply die. Since we do not want this to happen, today we will discuss how to wisely plan the production, transport, and distribution of edible goods 🍖 All right, it's time to visit Farmlands, Vineyards, Olive Groves, Bakeries, Granaries, Fishermen's huts, and Hunting lodges! As a ruler, you must make sure that their work is done quickly and efficiently.


[h2]Ways to feed the population[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Fortunately, there are numerous different ways to produce or obtain food. [b]Among the many buildings[/b] that you will have at your disposal as a ruler, you will soon find out that many of them are related to the production and storage of edible goods. The first two of them are the most primitive and closest to nature. Hunting Lodge and Fisherman's Hut 🐟 may not be too advanced, but [b]they perfectly serve their purpose[/b] of feeding your subjects from the very beginning of the game.

In the next stages, you will be able to use more advanced food producers such as Wheat, Cattle, or Goat Farm. Milk and wheat produced there can be [b]later processed into other goods[/b]. Thanks to them, various types of bakeries or the Cheesemaker's Hut can be built and operate in your city 🧀 

In addition to the above-mentioned, you can also use the services of Winery, Olive Grove, Grapevine Plantation, Vinegar Distillery, Slaughterhouse, or Brewery, which also deal with the production of edible goods. However, there's more - every good ruler should know [b]the great potential of trade[/b]. Remember that in case of a shortage of food in your city, you can always buy it from your neighbors ⚖ Crisis averted!


[h2]The more varied the better[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
While the main purpose of food is to keep your subjects alive, it is also [b]important when it comes to their well-being[/b]. Even the best, beloved dish will get boring if it is the only dish on our tables for a long time. With that in mind, remember that the more varied their diet is, the happier they are 😊 When expanding your city, make sure that it offers its inhabitants different types of meals. The rule is quite simple! If your granaries and warehouses are filled with a variety of edible goods, your subjects will repay you with loyalty and diligence! You know what they say - [b]a well-fed citizen is a good citizen![/b]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/13808a830ee9917e4d230e188291efe1cf868906.png[/img]

notes.title: Architect's Corner #6 - Odeon and Lesche
notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings Builders! 🏛️ [/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Welcome to the next part of our "Architect's Corner" series, in which we tell you all about the buildings you will have at your disposal as a ruler of an ancient Greek Polis. Discover interesting tips and tricks, learn how to effectively plan the development of your city, and check out how many useful structures you can raise - all this to the glory of a great ruler, such as yourself! 👑


[url=https://discord.gg/8KnCYpm2xT][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/2457a52332739537a74a64a1369ff6b89f30a2d4.png[/img][/url]
[h3]...and talk to the community and developers about the game![/h3]



[h2]Rest and recreation of your citizens[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
A hard day of work in a vineyard, sawmill, workshop or mine can take its toll... In such cases, your subjects will naturally long for a moment of respite and well-deserved rest 😴 And it is your job to meet these demands! 

Today, we will take a closer look at two unique places in which people of your Polis can regain their exhausted strength and refresh their minds. [b]Wise rulers know[/b] that the cultural and leisure needs of their subjects should not be taken lightly - in fact, they can significantly affect their level of satisfaction... and even [b]attitude towards your reign![/b]

[h2]Odeon[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Just a quick glance is enough to discover that the Odeon is a [b]place of high culture and art[/b]. A large, multi-story structure. Colorful columns, walls, and a tiled roof. Decorative statues and ornaments. When you stand at its door, it makes a truly stunning impression... and that's the goal! 🏛 One of Odeon's tasks is to provide your subjects with a sense of luxury, class, and grandeur. The real magic, however, begins after we cross its threshold...

The Odeon is where your townspeople can touch the eerie sphere of Sacrum and [b]delve into beautiful musical and theatrical performances[/b]. Knowing the history of Ancient Greece, we understand how much importance was once attached to this type of cultural events. The Odeons and Amphitheaters were regularly filled with crowds of viewers who wanted to see the acting representation of myths, historical events, and the most interesting stories of the time 📜


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/565c938d88ed5eee122d1e6c023c42ca9792165c.png[/img]


It is no different with your subjects who gather in the Odeon you have built. Thanks to the culture your subjects acquire in such places, they can [b]increase and improve their social status[/b]. This is especially important in the later stages of the game, when your city is already quite developed and needs noble families that increase its [b]prestige and wealth[/b] 🧐 Obviously, building an Odeon is not cheap, quick, or easy, but at some point, this investment will definitely pay off - be sure not to miss it!

[h2]Lesche[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Definitely less impressive and majestic... but still an equally important building! Wait - a simple, modest Lesche is just as necessary as the great Odeon? Well... of course! And this is why 😁

The majority of the society you will have an occasion to rule is made up of [b]lower social classes[/b]. We are talking about basic, rather simple workers, who spend their days in places such as mines, farms, non-specialized workshops, or granaries. Undoubtedly, these are difficult and tiring professions...

That being said, it should come as no surprise that this wide group of your subjects prefers [b]cheap and accessible kinds of recreation[/b]. And it just so happens that Lesche is one of them! 🍺 In fact, it's hard to find a better place to relax, grab something to eat, socialize with fellow citizens, and simply rest before the next day of hard work 🤝 The most important role of Lesche is to provide a refreshing meal to workers who are too far away from their homes during their working day. Such a visit saves a lot of time and energy!

Hosting dozens of guests, Lesche is constantly filled with sounds of laughter, cheerful conversations, and clanking of clay pots. It is true - it doesn't provide a deep cultural feeling like the Odeon, but[b] it definitely does its job![/b] 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/48685b0d480645bd5e7b5900d41be4d1132ad16b.png[/img]


Choosing the right place and building Lesche [b]will not be too difficult or expensive[/b]. It's an obvious advantage! You can easily place several of them among the streets of your city, to the delight of its inhabitants. You can be sure that your subjects will appreciate unfettered access to this tabernacle where they can rest and recharge their batteries! [b]Cheers! [/b] 🍻


In the following parts of the series, we will return with [b]descriptions of many other cool structures [/b]that will ensure the safety, well-being, and development of your city. notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings Builders! 🏛️ [/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Welcome to the next part of our "Architect's Corner" series, in which we tell you all about the buildings you will have at your disposal as a ruler of an ancient Greek Polis. Discover interesting tips and tricks, learn how to effectively plan the development of your city, and check out how many useful structures you can raise - all this to the glory of a great ruler, such as yourself! 👑


[url=https://discord.gg/8KnCYpm2xT][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/2457a52332739537a74a64a1369ff6b89f30a2d4.png[/img][/url]
[h3]...and talk to the community and developers about the game![/h3]


[h2]Thētes’ Houses[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
The foundation of the society you will happen to rule are tireless, hardworking and, telling the truth as it is, rather simple people. In Ancient Greece, they were called Thētes -  the lowest class of free men in the whole state, consisting mostly of poor peasants, small craftsmen, and landless hired workers ⚒️ The scope of their activities is therefore extremely wide and [b]essential for the survival of your city.[/b] You can meet Thētes in such places as farms, lumber mills, clay pits, olive groves, woodcutter's houses, fisherman's huts, hunting lodges, or varied kinds of minor workshops. Their hands may be blistered, and their necks sunburned, however, as long as you take good care of their needs, they will sure prove to be [b]loyal, well-performing subjects[/b].


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/fb41ec6a4e4d0bfc2ffd09cccc463067acb1bd95.png[/img]


Speaking of Thētes’s needs... one of the most important necessities of mankind is to have [b]shelter and a roof over their heads[/b]. The bigger, more comfortable, and well-stocked, the better! 🏛️ Thētes may not be a very demanding social layer, but still craves entertainment and access to a variety of goods. Anyhow, let's get back to the housing. As you can see in the illustration below, the Thētes' houses cannot be called very spacious and magnificent. The bodies of this type of buildings are [b]rather simple and austere[/b], they usually consist of a small number of rooms, and are quite low (two-story houses are in this case fairly rare). The roofs are most often covered with whitewashed stones or simple red tiles. Although such a house does not seem particularly cozy and roomy, [b]it fulfills its function perfectly[/b] - it provides safety and a place to live for numerous Thētes families. In the end, not everyone can live a comfortable, luxurious life of a ruler, right? 👑😁 

The construction of such simple houses does not require a lot of raw materials and work, so your builders will be able to build plenty of them in a short period of time. Thētes’ houses prove to be a great solution, whenever your city is experiencing a demographic surplus and needs to host numerous newcomers from all over Greece. Of course, with time, accumulated wealth, and access to demanded goods, [b]simple houses can advance to something more[/b] 💰 which leads us to...


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/76cc5af611beb3a53145f0a09197805172928940.png[/img]


[h2]Zeugitais’ Houses[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Zeugitai are wealthy enough to own a team of oxen... or to serve in famous hoplites formation. We are sure you get the idea - [b]this social layer is nothing else but the middle class[/b] of your population. Let's start with the fact, that Zeugitai are somewhat more qualified and demanding employees than the Thētes described above. They spend their working day in places such as watermills, more demanding farms like wheat farm, cattle farm, and flax plantation, or in different types of mines placed around your city. [b]Make no mistake[/b] - they still know how to work hard, but their job requires a bit more skill and experience ⛏️ As the goods and resources they produce are often quite valuable, they can afford a fairly comfortable standard of living. Take their homes as an example...


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/78b1ac1cabfd38f5365803a7c89d8e1d26a62a72.png[/img]


Zeugitai’s Houses are definitely more spacious and complex than cramped Thētes’ Houses - that's for sure! Middle class houses are covered with smooth, red tiles, they often have two floors, several rooms, and even a small, cozy porch. Zeugitai [b]families can enjoy more freedom and have some extra space[/b] to gather the goods they need in their everyday life 🚪 Naturally, building such a home is a bit more expensive and requires more work, however it is still a rather simple structure. When your Polis develops from a provincial town to a well-known, prosperous city, vacant space will be quickly filled with Zeugitais' houses... and the service buildings they crave for.

If you want [b]Zeugitai to feel comfortable in your city[/b], you need to provide them with the access not only to a variety of goods, but also to some class-fitting services. This social group loves to spend their free time in the Inn - a place where the latest news, rumors, and [b]matters important to the average citizen[/b] are discussed... not to mention the delicious beverages served there 🥃 In addition, it would be a wise decision to build the Ares Square. Thanks to this place, your dear Zeugitai will not only stay in good shape and practice their fighting skills, but also provide themselves with a great deal of entertainment! ⚔️ 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/6a44bef8b83738dc536c7f9dfcf1bf7c21622783.png[/img]


In the following parts of the series, we will return with [b]descriptions of many other cool structures [/b]that will ensure the safety, well-being, and development of your city. We hope that the buildings presented today will find their place among the streets of your Polis, and that they will contribute to the growth of [b]your magnificent kingdom![/b] 😀 As always - thank you and stay tuned!

notes.title: The Ruler's Manual #5 - Resources
notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings, mighty Builders! 🏛️ [/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Any ruler who wants to [b]go down in history[/b] 📚 should get acquainted with the "Ruler's Manual" series! Why - you ask? Well, in the following entries we tell you about how to make your Polis wealthy, safe, and as prosperous as possible. And believe us, it's [b]not as easy as it may seem! [/b]


[hr][/hr]
[url=https://discord.gg/8KnCYpm2xT][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/2457a52332739537a74a64a1369ff6b89f30a2d4.png[/img][/url]
[hr][/hr]
[h3]...and talk to the community and developers about the game![/h3]


Okay, let's get to the point, [b]shall we?[/b] Today's topic is of crucial importance to the well-being and even the very foundation of your city. 

[b]Raw resources[/b] - as we are going to talk about them - are not only the building blocks of your Polis, but also food for its inhabitants, crafting materials for its artisans, tradable goods for its merchants, and much, much more! Before you start collecting them, however, you must first get to know them... 🔍


[h2]Edible resources[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Without them, your Polis would be a ghost town. Constant access to food is something that every ruler must take care of 🍗 Edible resources include those coming from your farms, such as [b]Olives, Grapes, and Wheat[/b], which after proper preparation can find their place on the tables of your loyal citizens. However, this is not their only use! Example? Sure! Olives can be turned into medicines, perfumes, and bakery ingredients, Grapes are the basis of wine production, and Wheat, apart from the bread and tiganites bakery, is used in the brewery, stable, or goat and cattle farms. Quite useful, aren't they? 

Other resources in this category are materials of animal origin. These include [b]Poseidon's gift in the form of fish[/b] and milk that can be later processed into tasty, coveted cheese 🥛  This is a good moment to mention, that the varied diet (and that means providing yourself with several different sources of raw edible resources) makes your subjects happier and [b]more cooperative[/b] - keep that in mind while planning your production network! 🤔


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/b6634c76a8e8615b6037a9fbf654ea36f049552d.png[/img]


[h2]Building resources[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
When your subjects' bellies are full, you can take care of giving them a roof over their heads. To do this, you will need... (surprise, surprise) [b]raw resources![/b] Among the most important of them, we can name Wood and Stone. 🌳 On the one hand, you will need a lot of them - and we mean - a lot. On the other, they are [b]quite easy to collect and process[/b]. All around your city, you will find lush green forests as well as stone fields full of materials just waiting to gather them. To do that, you will need the Quarry, Woodcutter’s house ⛏️ and a bunch of strong workers!

With access to these building materials, your builders will be able to start their work. Ensure you have [b]sufficient supply of Wood, Stone, and (later on) Marble[/b], because they can be used in the production of many, many other goods. When the axes and pickaxes finally go into motion, your city will have everything it needs to grow and flourish! 🏛️


[h2]Mineral resources[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
It's time for a bit more sophisticated materials that can be used to make luxury goods such as [b]jewelry, weapons, tools, and many others[/b] ⚒️ In order to get them, you'll have to dig them out of the ground! Clay, Tin, Copper, Silver, and Gold are valuable resources that can be used in dozens of different ways... A wise ruler will see them as a valuable commodity for trade or a way to please the richer part of city dwellers. We believe you will find several other uses for them as well!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/0e9cc8eb31fb900b73fd84a8384034cbea16f4b7.png[/img]


Without raw mineral resources, your Polis will not reach a higher level of development and will remain just a small, provincial city. And this is not our goal, is it? Be sure, to[b] carefully browse your territory[/b] and find suitable places to build your mines and other gathering stations 🗺️ Sometimes different kinds of resources emerge from the ground, and you can always read it as a sign, that there is something valuable down there! notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings Builders! 🏛️ [/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Welcome to the next part of our "Architect's Corner" series, in which we tell you all about the buildings you will have at your disposal as a ruler of an ancient Greek Polis. Discover interesting tips and tricks, learn how to effectively plan the development of your city, and check out how many useful structures you can raise - all this to the glory of a great ruler, such as yourself! 👑


[url=https://discord.gg/8KnCYpm2xT][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/2457a52332739537a74a64a1369ff6b89f30a2d4.png[/img][/url]
[h3]...and talk to the community and developers about the game![/h3]


[h2]Warehouse[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Trolleys, barrels, ladders, and boxes... the Warehouse may not be the best looking building in your glorious city, however, its role is quite different. [b]And its beauty lies within[/b] 😁! How so? When citizens of your Polis set off to workshops, mines, and other labor facilities, they will produce numerous goods. These can be very basic resources like planks and tin ore, or more sophisticated products like furniture or perfumes - either way - they all need to find their way to the [b]Warehouse[/b].

When your workshops produce a certain amount of goods and reach their storage limits... [b]they will simply stop working![/b] We don't want that to happen, do we now? Collecting produced tools, wax tablets, lamps, wine, sculptures, herbs, or other goods is always a good idea - a well-stocked Warehouse allows you to survive more difficult times (such as war, riots, natural disasters), but also makes you a [b]promising trade partner![/b]

Now that you know how important the Warehouse is to the economy of your city, [b]remember to build it in a right place[/b]. If production or service buildings are within range of the Warehouse, your subjects will take care of the automatic transport of goods. [b]Another tip[/b] is to build a thoughtful road network. All of your workshops have to be connected to the Warehouse, otherwise storage will not be possible! And hey - don't hesitate to build a few Warehouses if your city's production is in full swing... "plenty is no plague", as they say 🤑


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/cf547f5ba4af270b03a4c86b25b176f85c0eb390.png[/img]


[h2]Clay Pit[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
As we all know, Ancient Greeks had a soft spot for pottery 😁 The museums are full of [b]beautiful pots, vases, and amphoras[/b] depicting scenes from their everyday lives, mythical heroes, and important historical events. There is a lot of evidence that clay pots can become real works of art, but they also fulfill another, more practical, yet simple function - namely, they are great containers! All right, let's follow the path the clay mined in your Pit goes through.

As you can probably guess, working in a place such as a Clay Pit is not very comfortable and pleasant, however scorching sun, dirt, and hard physical labor are not enough to put your workers off! You will need up to five of them, as the [b]Clay Pit is a rather big building[/b]. Before you decide to build it, make sure that you have found the right place. The Clay Pit won't work if not placed on a clay field - be sure to look for it in the surroundings of your City! Once it is built in the right place and gets its staff allocation, raw clay can begin its second life.

The first building that cannot do without the support of a Clay Pit is, of course,[b] the Ceramics workshop. [/b]This is where raw clay is formed and processed into ceramics - [b]one of the most useful goods[/b] in ancient Polis ⚖️ Clay pitchers and pots are essential to the operation of many essential facilities in your City - Perfumery, Winery, Olive Press, or Brewery are just to begin with! In general, ceramics will be needed wherever liquid and loose products are made. That being said, [b]production in your city can get stuck for good [/b]if you don't supply the workshops with the right amount of ceramics. Such a close network of cooperation means that problems in the Clay Pit can have a bearing on your entire kingdom, so... don't spare a penny to build several Clay Pits in your area! Although they seem inconspicuous, they are very, very important!

notes.title: The Ruler's Manual #4 - Trade
notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings, mighty Rulers! 🏛️ [/h1]
[hr][/hr]
Even the most powerful and magnificent city must take into account its neighbors. And it's not just about making alliances or declaring wars. Many believe that trading is one of the fastest ways to earn [b]significant wealth [/b]and gain promising influence 👑 This statement may turn out to be true... as long as several important conditions are met.

Today, we're going to tell you all about the advantages and challenges of trading with other city-states. If you prove to be a skillful merchant, fame and wealth await you. If you don't prepare properly, however, your city may soon run out of many essential goods. The stakes are high! 💰


[url=https://discord.gg/8KnCYpm2xT][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/2457a52332739537a74a64a1369ff6b89f30a2d4.png[/img][/url]
[h3]...and talk to the community and developers about the game![/h3]


[h2]Basics of trade and exchange of goods[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
The basis of trade is adequate infrastructure. No caravan or merchant ship will come to your city unless you prepare a place for them to stay and present their goods. That being said, make sure your Polis has no shortage of [b]Trading Posts and a Harbor[/b]. Additionally, the mentioned Trading Posts must be connected with roads that will allow foreign merchants to reach your city.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/9bcb341b418f435cd8e876c9ee18381f04b53c15.png[/img]
[i]You can build a Harbor on one of the shores near your city[/i]


Now that you have built the necessary buildings, you can invite traders from other kingdoms. To do so, sign a commercial contract with your neighbors. Be careful! Only those with whom you have a [b]good relationship[/b] will agree to make such a commitment 🤝 If all goes to plan, the first merchants will soon appear on the horizon.

[h2]How to get rich?[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
When a merchant ship enters your harbor, or a caravan arrives at your Trading Post, you will be informed by a special notification. And [b]this is where the magic begins![/b] After opening the notification, you will see the trade panel. Thanks to this panel, you will learn what kind of wares the merchant offers, what he requests in return, and what amount of goods he has in stock.

The trade panel is divided into two parts - one representing your goods and the other showing the trader's goods ⚖️ By using special arrows near the wares symbol, you can decide [b]what kind and how many goods you want to buy or sell[/b]. Will you sell planks this time? Or maybe lamps? Is it worth buying fish? It all depends entirely on you! Remember that different traders will be interested in different offers - for example, some kingdoms will be willing to pay more for tools, while others may not pay attention to them at all.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/05562f4ea8e1d7337636a6f6858bcc3f4570102a.png[/img]
[i]No good Polis can do without a Marketplace[/i]


Once you have decided what goods you want to exchange, you will see a summary of the transaction cost at the bottom of the panel. Make sure the exchange will be to your advantage (whether in commodities or in drahmas)! 😉 Once you master the art of negotiation, you can simply use the [b]auto-trade option.[/b]

[h2]Benefits for your treasury and subjects[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Now it's time for the [b]most enjoyable part - the profits![/b] Your subjects will undoubtedly appreciate the exotic, coveted goods that you acquired by trading. Their constant influx can raise citizens' level of satisfaction and improve their life in general. In addition, thoughtful, wise trading can be the source of great wealth. If you produce a surplus of a certain commodity, don't hesitate to put it on the market - instead of wasting in your warehouses, it can turn into [b]valuable, shiny coins[/b]! 😁

notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings Builders! 🏛️ [/h1]
[hr][/hr]
[h3]Welcome to a brand-new series in which we will tell you all about the buildings you will have at your disposal as a ruler of an ancient Greek Polis.[/h3] 

At first glance, the buildings we are discussing today belong to the category of food producers... and that is, in a way, true. However, they are [b]definitely more than that![/b] 🍗 You will soon find out that the presence of a Hunting Lodge and Olive Press is essential not only to feed your loyal subjects, but also to guarantee them access to slightly more luxurious goods and to ensure their overall well-being. [h2]Hunting Lodge[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Hunting wild animals is one of [b]the oldest ways of obtaining food in the world[/b]. 🏹 The ancient Greeks knew this very well, so they often went on hunting trips in search of deer, rabbits, boars, and other wildlife that could replenish their reserves of fresh meat. With the use of bows and javelins, they tried to provide their kin with [b]a warm, nutritious meal.[/b]

You too can rely on the skills of your hunters and build their modest outpost - a Hunting Lodge. Be sure to place it near the forest... for obvious reason. The meat they will provide to your Polis may prove to be a very important element of the welfare of your subjects. Remember that a varied diet consisting of different types of food has [b]a positive effect on the morale of your citizens.[/b] When meat doesn't show up in their pantries often enough, their attitude towards you may deteriorate! Remember - a hungry citizen is a querulous citizen! 😣

Luckily, the Hunting Lodge is a rather [b]simple and cheap building[/b]. Moreover, you will be able to build it right away, just after starting the game, so feel free to stockpile meat from the very beginning of your reign. You will need up to three employees to make sure your Hunting Lodge is working efficiently.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/98860ec332fe1bc0298d6e1a09f2ae548aaefefc.png[/img]

The Olive Press is a slightly larger and more advanced building than the Hunting Lodge, so naturally it's a bit more expensive to build and maintain. However, this should not put you off! The olives delivered from the olive groves are crushed with a huge press, and the resulting [b]oil is collected [/b]to be used in further production. You will need three employees to operate the press.

Lampmaker's hut, Tiganites bakery, Cosmetic, and Pharmacist workshops - all of these buildings are dependent on the efficient work of the Olive Press. notes.title: The Ruler's Manual #3 - Citizens' Happiness
notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings, mighty Rulers! 🏛️ [/h1]
[hr][/hr]

[b]Buildings, streets, farms, or workshops may be very important, however it is the citizens who are really essential for your reigns and breathe life into your Polis.[/b] After all, they carry out numerous tasks, trade, erect new structures, cultivate the land, and fight in your name. Your subjects will have no problem with serving a wise, good ruler... but this situation can quickly reverse if they are not satisfied.



[url=https://discord.gg/8KnCYpm2xT][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/2457a52332739537a74a64a1369ff6b89f30a2d4.png[/img][/url]
[h3]...and talk to the community and developers about the game![/h3]



[h2]A happy citizen is a good citizen[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
This rule should guide you throughout your whole adventure with Builders of Greece. Suffice it to say that a [b]bad attitude towards your subjects[/b] can prove disastrous and lead to your end... sounds terrible, doesn't it? 😰 This is why taking care of your citizens' happiness and needs are so important! Today we are going to tell you how can you win their love and hearts, so that you can go down in history as a great and generous ruler! 👑


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/46bad59f0fc4cabd45195a44037303e7495e3553.gif[/img]


[h2]Food, services... and?[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
When your [b]granaries run out of food[/b], know that you are in trouble. It should come as no surprise that famine is very bad for the morale of your citizens! The first thing you should take care of is to make sure that their stomachs are never empty. Free access to fresh water is equally important. Place a few Water Pumps in the streets of your city to quench the thirst of its inhabitants. 💧 Meeting these basic needs may not make your subjects completely happy, but it is essential to further improving their level of satisfaction.

Another important thing is to look after [b]their other, more complex demands[/b] - you have to remember to grant them access to more luxurious goods such as lamps or furniture. Various types of service buildings may also prove to be useful here - your subjects will surely appreciate the possibility to go to the Inn, have some fun at the Stadium, or pay a visit to a nearby Healer's house.

The latter can be of great importance, because the inhabitants of your Polis will be happier if you take care of the [b]proper level of hygiene and overall health[/b] of your city. It's hard to blame them - the specter of an impending plague can spoil even the best of moods. In addition, their level of satisfaction is influenced by taxes and war... but this is a topic for a completely different article 😉


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/a6057266bdb1a18fb41066ef1dfdf826ebaab4d5.gif[/img]


[h2]What can you gain, what can you lose[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Okay, now that we've told you how to keep your people happy, we need to think about the consequences of their happiness or misery. [b]Let's start with the positives![/b] Satisfied residents can significantly increase their productivity, thanks to which they can fulfill their duties much faster. But that's not all - inhabitants of the surrounding territories will soon find out how well is your city doing and may decide to settle in it! Needles to say, it is very important for the further development of your Polis! Moreover, happy residents with satisfied needs will climb up the social ladder and improve their households.

On the other hand, dissatisfied or even enraged subjects can turn out to be very troublesome! Not only will they slow down their work, sabotage productivity, and spread the word that your city is not worth living in, but they will also (at some point, when their anger reaches its zenith) start setting buildings on fire! 🔥 Such a situation can lead to many unpleasant events - breaking the supply chain, abandoning houses, reduced profits from trading, or even hunger.

As you can see, citizens' happiness is an extremely important element of the game. Efficient rulers cannot overlook their subjects' moods, so always keep an eye on their satisfaction level! Luckily, now you know how to deal with them all!

notes.title: The Ruler's Manual #2 - Faith
notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings Builders! 🏛️ [/h1]
[hr][/hr]
[h3]In today's devlog we will discuss the importance of faith in Ancient Greece in the Pantheon of Greek Gods, highlighting the twelve gods who lived on the top of Mount Olympus.[/h3]

[h2]Faith in Ancient Greece[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
[b]Due to the need to explain the action and the reason for the existence of supernatural phenomena, the world of Greek gods, full of inspiration and ingenuity, was unrivaled in relation to the contemporary systems of faiths.[/b]

The myths of the Greeks tell not only about the great deeds of gods and heroes, but also explain the current state of the world, its history reaching even its origin, and explain phenomena occurring, which are both a huge inspiration for poets, painters, and philosophers, and the meaning of existence for ordinary people. Myths also teach how to act in life, what deeds are conducive to, and what are condemned. The importance of faith is emphasized by its influence on almost every element of Greek culture. Buildings and statues were created in honor of the gods, which were important not only in architecture. The creation of an ancient theater in honor of the god Dionysus laid the foundations for new forms of art such as tragedy, comedy, and drama. Many artists drew inspiration from the gods to create their amazing songs, sculptures, paintings, and other works.

The inhabitants of Ancient Greece worshiped the gods in dedicated altars, temples, or other places marked with the symbolism of a specific god. Cultivating faith did not depend on social strata. Each resident, regardless of his status and property, cared about worshiping the gods for the sake of safety, health, and prosperity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/ff1f26fc261fd8fef6b0ce9c6731dae85c3cf263.png[/img]

To this day, the strong influence of the extremely deep belief system of the Greeks can be seen in the artistic work of various nations. Undeniable, even classic mythological motifs, the sources of which should be sought in antiquity, today constitute a canon that every enlightened person knows.

[h2]Olympian Gods[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
[b]In ancient Greek religion and mythology, the twelve gods form the core of all pantheon mythology.[/b]

They were called Olympian gods because they lived on top of Mount Olympus. They decided on almost all significant issues in the world, including the existence, life, and death of people. The gods drank divine nectar and ate ambrosia, which gave them eternal life and enduring beauty.

The twelve gods of Olympus are composed of*:

[list]
[*][b]Zeus[/b] - the god of heaven and thunder, the highest of all gods
[*][b]Poseidon[/b] - god of rivers, lakes, seas and oceans, brother of Zeus
[*][b]Hera[/b] - goddess of marriage, queen of heaven, wife of Zeus
[*][b]Ares[/b] - god of bloody war
[*][b]Apollo[/b] - god of poetry, dance and music
[*][b]Aphrodite[/b] - goddess of love, beauty and procreation
[*][b]Hephaestus[/b] - god of fire, blacksmiths and goldsmiths
[*][b]Dionysus[/b] - god of grape-harvest and wine
[*][b]Hermes[/b] - a divine herald, guardian of traders and travelers
[*][b]Demeter[/b] - goddess of crops and harvest
[*][b]Athena[/b] - goddess of wisdom and battle
[*][b]Artemis[/b] - goddess of the hunt and the wild
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/b423584f2d0e8d59e5eb9869f06b7289f6d3a094.png[/img]

Although [b]Hades[/b] was one of the chief gods of ancient Greece and was the brother of Zeus and Poseidon himself, his kingdom was the underworld, far from Olympus, and thus was not considered by many to be one of the Olympian gods. Despite this, its significance was enormous in the daily lives of the inhabitants who hoped that their dead would reach the [b]Champs-Elysées[/b] and not be thrown into the dark [b]Tartarus[/b].

[i]* - Fun fact: not all source materials define the composition of the twelve Olympic gods equally. The materials are compatible with ten gods: Aphrodite, Apollo, Ares, Artemis, Athena, Hephaestus, Hera, Hermes, Poseidon, and Zeus. The other two places, depending on the sources, are complemented by: Hades, Demeter, Dionysus, and Hestia.[/i]

[h2]The importance of faith in the game[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
[b] In Builders of Greece you can pay tribute to each of the Olympic gods, directing his favor to your Polis and protecting yourself from his wrath. [/b]

When building places of worship, decide which gods will be worshiped by the inhabitants of your polis and what effects their prayers will bring. The gods mentioned in the previous paragraph will appear as potential cult units. 

Several buildings will appear in the game that will serve as places of worship. The most important of them are [b]altars[/b] and [b]temples[/b]. The altar, being simple to build and small building, can at a low cost provide the inhabitants with the need to pray and cultivate the faith, and the ruler can guarantee the favor of a specific god. Temples are much larger structures that require much more resources and time to build while providing much better results than altars. For buildings of faith to function properly, they must have a specific deity to whom they will be dedicated and for whom the inhabitants of the polis will pray.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/27cf017176759f26c527051759074e0bbf83aefa.png[/img]

Using faith buildings, we can perform a variety of rituals, such as prayer, ritual sacrifice in the form of crops, liquids, or animals, and even performing the [b]Hecatomb[/b].

Each ritual will require the appropriate materials to perform it. The completed ritual will provide the appropriate effects, depending on the deity towards which the ritual was directed, and will ensure his favor. For example, by performing a ritual in honor of [b]Demeter[/b], a blessing can be sent to the player, which will increase the yield of farmland and the number of successful catches, and in addition, Demeter will be more accommodating to the player, which can reduce the frequency of droughts and crop failure.

The more we focus on the glory of a god, the more he will be in favor of our actions. It should be remembered that each of the gods has its own requirements, desires, and attributes, and the fate of our polis and the ancient world largely depends on them. Having the favor of the gods is always better for the people and the ruler than not having it.

notes.title: The Ruler's Manual #1 - Social strata
notes.content:
[h1] 🏛️ Greetings Builders! 🏛️ [/h1]

[b]We present you with the latest information from the game. Today we will talk about the social strata and the importance of society in Ancient Greece and also in the game.[/b]


[url=https://discord.gg/8KnCYpm2xT][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/2457a52332739537a74a64a1369ff6b89f30a2d4.png[/img][/url]
[h3]...and talk with the community and devs about the game![/h3]


According to history, the population in the game will be divided not only according to their social status but also according to their needs. To be successful, you need to keep society happy. It is only up to you whether your policy will be able to meet the requirements of each resident, from the poorest to the richest.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/9cedb4613b7f21ac35b89ee51aee19b4f107ee37.png[/img]

Depending on their status and satisfaction, the population will be able to migrate between social strata so as to successfully build districts of various traits in the polis. Each apartment building, after meeting the relevant requirements, can be improved so that its inhabitants can transfer their social status to a higher level. Houses inhabited by each of the social classes are characterized by a unique style and represent their property status. 

[h3]There are four basic social layers during the game:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Thetes [/b] - They are the lowest class of society which is made up of a wide variety of members, mainly poor peasants, small craftsmen, and landless hired workers. The thetes were made up of citizens with property producing less than 200 medimnos* of grain a year.
[*] [b]Zeugitai [/b] - The class to which the famous hoplites belonged. The representative of Zeugitai was wealthy enough to own a team of oxen. Their fortune did not exceed 300 medimnos of grain a year.
[*] [b]Hippeis [/b] - Mostly known as Greek cavalry and the second most prosperous social group, initially consisting of those who could afford a horse and rider's equipment. Later, the definition of hippeis as a social group broke away from the possibility of undertaking horse service in the army.
[*] [b]Pentakosiomedimnoi [/b] - "Five-hundred-bushel men" refers to the richest people whose annual grain income exceeded 500 medimnos. Members of the social class also obtained the right to run for the office of the archon.
[/list]
[i]*A medimnos was an Ancient Greek unit of volume  = 1 bushel = 8 dry gallons = around 52 liters.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/79d46e30a4d07f6869c4349608cb2102f46e6797.png[/img]

Each resident of Polis, climbing up the hierarchy, changes his requirements and profession. The names of the social strata come from the historical division of Ancient Greece society and reflect the professional divisions.

Increasing the qualifications and social status not only allows the use of the new potential for new jobs and activities but will also be associated with greater citizen requirements. In our game, citizens when changing their social status also changes the building in which they live, the goods they need and the and the requirements they have towards the ruler. The sustainable development of your Polis is also important so that everyone is satisfied.

Meeting the demands of your people is a key part of keeping your inhabitants happy. Remember to always provide them with the appropriate goods, because the satisfaction of the inhabitants is the foundation of a prospering and united polis. Thanks to the different tiers of society, the game reflects the complexity of the social structures of Ancient Greece. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37828759/716030237998aa3f3792cd49c19b18d2d34a32e1.png[/img]

In the Ancient Greek world, religion was personal, direct, and present in all areas of your citizens' life, which makes it one of the most important element of their happiness. It is only up to you which gods will send grace to your polis and which will send their anger. A series of random events and consequences of the player's actions cause the world of ancient Greek polis to be filled with the will of the Olympian Gods.

In the next episode, we will talk more about the religion in the game and the possibility of worshiping the gods of Olympus
